sheets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ORIGINAL modular 3D asset-family modeling reference sheet for a Blender artist/coding agent. The two attached images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: match their middle-ground grounded low-poly geometry and modest worn texture detail; do not copy their lighthouse, garage, map layout, BMW or specific architecture. Design new unbranded assets for an original racing map, inspired only by the gritty autumn industrial atmosphere of NFS Most Wanted (2005) and the layered urban/industrial road shapes of NFS Carbon. Realistic proportions and functional construction. Angular substantial structural masses, natural limited shading, matte muted beige/gray concrete, dark steel, subdued russet brick, sparse broad wear. Enough seams and openings to recognize the material, but no photographic microtexture, modeled bricks, tiny fasteners, heavy grunge, glossy promotional render, toy/chibi/miniature proportions, crystalline blockout look, cel outlines, voxel shapes or copied franchise landmarks. Presentation: one wide 16:9 contact sheet on a plain muted warm-gray background with simple soft cast shadows. Objects separated cleanly, all boundaries visible, no scenic backdrop, no vehicles or people. Main asset shown from a clear front-three-quarter angle and a matching rear-three-quarter angle; smaller constituent modules shown separately in an orderly lower strip. Use gentle consistent diffuse light so silhouette and material separation are easy to study. No perspective exaggeration, depth of field, motion blur, neon, decorative frames, logos, text, labels, dimension arrows, watermarks or UI. Matching views must depict the same new design. This is a visual modeling target, not engineering drawing; guide dimensions will be supplied separately. Family: two-lane asphalt ROAD SEGMENTS and sidewalk kit. Main modules shown from elevated three-quarter and near-plan views: a 16-metre straight segment with paired 3.5-metre lanes and a smooth broad 45-degree bend, each with sparse faded double-yellow center marking and thin white edge marking. Dry dark gray asphalt with a few broad quiet repairs. Lower strip: separate short curb section, sidewalk slab strip, beveled driveway curb and asphalt-to-dirt shoulder. Show actual construction thickness and connecting cross-sections; endpoints are straight, matching road cross-sections. Bends must be curves with moderate segment count, not jagged corners. The main straight/bend modules are separated objects, not a diorama.
